def process(roman_cities, world_cities) -> pd.DataFrame:
    rc = roman_cities[['Primary Key','Longitude (X)','Latitude (Y)']].dropna()
    wc = world_cities[['id','city','lat','lng','population']].dropna(subset=['lat','lng','population'])
    wc = wc[wc['population'] > 100000]
    wc['__k'] = 1
    rc['__k'] = 1
    df = pd.merge(wc, rc, on='__k').drop('__k', axis=1)
    df['dist_deg'] = ((df['lat'] - df['Latitude (Y)'])**2 + (df['lng'] - df['Longitude (X)'])**2)**0.5
    df = df[df['dist_deg'] <= 0.1]
    result = pd.DataFrame({'modern_city_count': [df['id'].nunique()]})
    return result
input.summary: Filter world_cities to population >100000 and roman_cities to rows with coords; perform cross-join and compute Euclidean distance in degrees between (lat,lng) and (Latitude (Y), Longitude (X)); keep pairs with distance <= 0.1 degrees; return number of unique modern city ids as column modern_city_count.
